name: Industrial and Systems Engineering
description: Industrial engineering programmes teach the design and improvement of systems that combine people, machines, materials and information — production lines, supply chains, hospitals, airports and theme parks. It is the engineering discipline least tied to one industry, and the one whose graduates most often end up running operations.
degreesNote: A Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering — often titled Industrial and Systems Engineering — with master’s and doctoral degrees above it. ⚠ Four Florida public institutions award the bachelor’s, so the undergraduate footprint is small; systems engineering is filed under its own code and is largely a master’s and certificate offering for people already working. The degree should come from a programme accredited by ABET’s ENGINEERING commission if a Professional Engineer licence is ever the goal, though industrial engineers are licensed less often than civil engineers because most of the work falls under the industry exemption.

cips.note: Industrial Engineering — the degree itself. Four Florida public institutions award it, at every level from bachelor’s through doctorate.

Systems Engineering — filed separately by five Florida institutions and awarded mostly at master’s and certificate level. ⚠ Included deliberately: Florida departments routinely teach the two as one programme ("Industrial and Systems Engineering"), and filing under 14.35 alone would hide institutions that teach the subject.

related.note: ⚠ The realistic alternative where no industrial degree is nearby — it is awarded at eleven institutions against four — and manufacturing, ergonomics and operations work is open to both. Mechanical designs the machine; industrial designs the system around it.

The adjacent route, and relevant here because a sizeable share of people enter this occupation from the floor rather than from a degree. Engineering technology programmes are how many of them formalise what they already do.
